justification: Adds a production trigger on the three rule tables that logs every protected change with its pipeline run, tags the eleven pipeline writers, and blocks scratchpad scripts that write rule tables

falsifiable_check.command: python -m pytest tests/test_rule_write_guard_db.py tests/test_scratchpad_rule_write_guard.py (DB tests in CI job drawdown-verify-write-path, isolated Postgres)
falsifiable_check.fails_when: an untagged UPDATE of source_text or a self-stamped verbatim release succeeds in enforce mode, or a real batch writer script is allowed by the hook
falsifiable_check.observed_red: before the posix=False fix, test_the_real_batch1_writer_from_a_scratchpad_is_blocked failed with assert (0 == 2): the hook allowed C:\Users\...\write_batch1.py because shlex posix mode stripped the backslashes

pre_impl.existing_data: dcp_setback_controls 1273 rows, dcp_chapter_registry 822, regulatory_provisions 55k; trigger dcp_setback_hold_unproven_quote trusts the writer-sent quote_status; all connections are the postgres superuser
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: PGOPTIONS would have tagged every connection in one place, but the Supabase pooler drops startup options (measured: current_setting returned None), so each connect site tags itself
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: adds one trigger function and two tables; reuses the existing isolated Postgres CI job and the existing hook registration and hook-health test
pre_impl.external_source_error: if set_config fails the connect site raises and the pipeline run stops before any write, which is loud rather than an untagged write
pre_impl.frontend_type: none: no API or UI reads rule_write_log or rule_write_guard in this change
pre_impl.user_failure_mode: in record mode nothing is refused, so a missed writer shows up as run_id IS NULL rows in rule_write_log rather than as a broken job

functions.name: run_id
functions.input: the pipeline script name as given by the calling script
functions.output: a run id made of script name, twelve-character git sha and a twelve-character random run part
functions.if_none: a blank or None script name raises ValueError so no run is ever logged under an empty name

functions.name: tag
functions.input: an open psycopg2 connection object and the name of the calling pipeline script
functions.output: the run id after setting app.pipeline_run and application_name on that database session
functions.if_none: a connection that is not psycopg2 gets no SQL at all and the run id is still returned to the caller

functions.name: _git_sha
functions.input: nothing beyond the environment and the checkout this file sits in
functions.output: the first twelve characters of the deployed or checked-out git commit hash
functions.if_none: with no Railway variable and no git it returns unknown and tag prints a warning on stderr

functions.name: verdict
functions.input: the shell command text with its working directory and the repository root path
functions.output: None to let the command run, or the reason string that makes the hook block it
functions.if_none: a command that runs no python and names no .py script returns None without reading any file

functions.name: _tracked
functions.input: the resolved script path and the repository root used for git commands
functions.output: True only when git says the file is tracked and has no uncommitted change
functions.if_none: git missing, hung or failing returns False so the file is read rather than trusted

functions.name: _scripts
functions.input: the full shell command, possibly several commands joined by shell separators
functions.output: every .py path that any python invocation or shebang run in the command names
functions.if_none: a command with no python and no leading .py word returns an empty list of scripts

break_it.scenario: scratchpad script UPDATEs source_text directly, as batches 1-5 did
break_it.what_happens: the rule text changes with no run behind it
break_it.how: hook blocks the run; in enforce mode the trigger refuses it; in record mode it is logged with run_id NULL
break_it.repro: pytest tests/test_rule_write_guard_db.py -k scratchpad (CI) and tests/test_scratchpad_rule_write_guard.py -k batch1

break_it.scenario: script stamps quote_status verbatim and needs_review false on its own row
break_it.what_happens: migration 120 trusts the stamp and the row is served
break_it.how: enforce mode refuses the change with no run

break_it.scenario: extractor reconnects mid-run or commit job starts council_quote as a child
break_it.what_happens: the second connection would carry a different or no run id
break_it.how: tag reuses PIPELINE_RUN_ID from the environment for the whole process tree

break_it.scenario: a script sets app.pipeline_run to an empty string before writing
break_it.what_happens: an empty tag would count as a tagged pipeline write and pass
break_it.how: nullif treats empty as no run

break_it.scenario: the scratchpad script path is given with Windows backslashes or a git-bash drive
break_it.what_happens: the hook could not find the file and allowed it
break_it.how: shlex posix=False plus git-bash drive path conversion; tested on 8 real scripts

break_it.scenario: a tracked repo script that is not pipeline writes the tables
break_it.what_happens: the hook allows it and the write lands with no run named
break_it.how: by design: tracked code is reviewed, and the trigger logs it with run_id NULL; enforce mode will refuse it after the record week
break_it.repro: SELECT count(*) FROM rule_write_log WHERE run_id IS NULL

break_it.scenario: an untagged script deletes or truncates rule rows instead of updating them
break_it.what_happens: the rule disappears from served results with no log line
break_it.how: Sol finding 1: DELETE row trigger logs by OLD and TRUNCATE statement trigger; both refused in enforce

break_it.scenario: a scratchpad writer is the second python command in a chained shell line
break_it.what_happens: the hook read only the first python and allowed the writer
break_it.how: Sol finding 2: split on ; && || | and newline, read every invocation

break_it.scenario: the migration ships in record mode so an untagged release still succeeds
break_it.what_happens: a bad write is logged with run_id NULL but not stopped for the record week
break_it.how: VERDICT on Sol finding 3: kept. Enforcing before measuring would break unknown jobs among 137 writer files; record mode is no weaker than today; the hook blocks the session route that made batches 1-5. Enforce after rule_write_log shows 0 untagged pipeline writes for 7 days
break_it.repro: SELECT count(*) FROM rule_write_log WHERE run_id IS NULL AND at > now() - interval '7 days'

break_it.scenario: an untagged writer rewrites plain_summary that users read
break_it.what_happens: user-facing wording changes with no log and no refusal
break_it.how: Sol finding 4: plain_summary added to the protected columns

break_it.scenario: tag leaves a transaction open and the extractor then sets conn.autocommit
break_it.what_happens: psycopg2 raises and the extract run dies at start-up
break_it.how: Sol finding 5: tag commits the transaction its own SELECT opened

break_it.scenario: the singleton rule_write_guard row is deleted after enforce is switched on
break_it.what_happens: the mode read as NULL and untagged writes went through unrefused
break_it.how: Sol round 2: coalesce(mode,'enforce') so a missing row fails closed

break_it.scenario: python is called with an option that takes a value such as -W ignore
break_it.what_happens: the hook took the option value as the script and allowed the writer
break_it.how: Sol round 2: every .py word in the python command is read

break_it.scenario: a tracked repo script is edited to add a rule-table write and run before commit
break_it.what_happens: the hook trusted any tracked path and the unreviewed write ran
break_it.how: Sol round 3: tracked is trusted only when git diff HEAD shows no change

break_it.scenario: the writer file is created and run inside the same shell command
break_it.what_happens: the file did not exist when the hook looked so it was allowed
break_it.how: Sol round 3: a named .py that does not exist yet blocks when the command carries rule-table SQL

break_it.scenario: a scratchpad writer is run directly through its shebang line without python
break_it.what_happens: no python word in the command so the hook did not look
break_it.how: Sol round 3: a segment that starts with a .py path is read like a python run

break_it.scenario: a writer is hidden on purpose, base64-decoded or loaded with exec(open(...)) inside python -c
break_it.what_happens: the hook sees no SQL and no readable script and allows it
break_it.how: VERDICT on Sol round 4 findings 2-3: out of scope. The hook catches accidental scratchpad writes (all 8 real ones blocked); it reads commands and cannot defeat deliberate obfuscation. The control for that is migration 121 in enforce mode, which refuses any untagged write whatever produced it. Round 4 finding 1 is the record-mode decision already recorded.
break_it.repro: SELECT count(*) FROM rule_write_log WHERE run_id IS NULL

break_it.scenario: python gets an option before -c, or VAR=x comes before a shebang script
break_it.what_happens: the inline or shebang check did not match and the writer ran
break_it.how: Sol round 5: options allowed before -c and -, VAR=x words skipped

break_it.scenario: python is called by a venv or absolute path, or the SQL quotes the table name
break_it.what_happens: the interpreter or the table did not match and the writer ran
break_it.how: Sol round 6: path separators and quotes accepted before python, quoted identifiers matched; python -m on a scratch module is a recorded limit covered by the DB guard

post_merge.manual_verify: Yes - apply migration 121 to production after a backup (needs the user's go), then confirm rule_write_log fills from the next pipeline run

real_layer_exempt.scripts/pipeline_run.py: its real-database tests are in tests/test_rule_write_guard_db.py (tag against a real Postgres, autocommit after tag, run id in rule_write_log), run by the CI isolated-DB job
real_layer_exempt.scripts/add_new_chapter.py: the only change is one pipeline_run.tag call after connect; the tag itself is real-DB tested in tests/test_rule_write_guard_db.py

qa_verify.mutations_run: hook: always-allow 13/17 fail, never-match-SQL 13/17, trust-all-tracked 11/17, no-shell-split 1/17, posix-split 8/17, no-shebang 2/17, always-block 5/17. pipeline_run: no-reuse, no-blank-check, no-warn, no-real-check, short-sha each caught. DB tests (CI only): reasoned, not run locally.
qa_verify.gaps_decided: TRUNCATE in record mode is not tested on its own (same code path as the enforce test). python -m <scratch module> is not caught by the hook (recorded limit, DB guard covers it). Stub tables carry only the columns the trigger reads; the install-time column check runs again against the real tables when migration 121 is applied.
